attributes.residual: The rule stays; this record is the source-exhaustion provenance it did not have. THE MECHANISM, from the aligned raw view. Nine FPRs are live in each stream (f0-f8 in both, so there is NO pressure asymmetry - this is the check that distinguishes this function from the eleven-versus-ten story attempt.PP_pointlinedist2d... left as its next step, and it comes out NEGATIVE here). The whole 40-word gap is which register carries the loop-carried MINIMUM accumulator. Retail reserves f0 for it (`@0x14 lfs f0,lbl_803468B0` = the 100000.0f seed, `@0xc0 fcmpo cr0,f6,f0`, `@0xcc fmr f0,f6`) and pushes the three loop-invariant constants to f5/f4/f3 and the loop scratch to f1,f2,f6,f7,f8. Ours puts the accumulator in f6 (`@0x14 lfs f6`, `@0xc0 fcmpo cr0,f5,f6`, `@0xcc fmr f6,f5`), the constants to f4/f3/f2 and uses f0 itself as loop scratch. So the single decision is whether f0 - MWCC's habitual scratch register - is reserved across the loop for a loop-carried value; retail's allocator reserved it and ours does not. Note also, for a pool lane and NOT for this residual: retail's four constants come from named .sdata2 objects at non-consecutive addresses (lbl_803468B0, lbl_80346820, lbl_80346830, lbl_803468B8), i.e. TU-shared pool entries, while ours emits four fresh per-function anonymous entries @1058-@1061. `wf_word_diff` reports RELOC-SYMBOL MISMATCH = 0, so those rows cost no differing words and are not part of this cap.

denial.falsifier: Any source form of fn_80051480 that makes MWCC reserve f0 across the loop for `best_dist` while keeping 58 instructions.
denial.premise_measurement: Two `ninja -j2 build/GUNE5D/src/game/game/.postprocess/body/gamemain.o` rebuilds scored with `wf_word_diff.py game/game/gamemain fn_80051480`: HEAD 40 words, `register` removed 40 words with a byte-identical aligned view over 0x10:0x40, block-locals hoisted 40 words.
denial.scope: The `register` storage-class axis and the block-scope-versus-function-scope declaration axis on fn_80051480 only. It does NOT deny the live-range axis or the constant-pool axis named in `hypothesis`, neither of which was tried.

held_fixed: The `volatile f32 tmp;` inside the guarded block (which produces the +0xb8 stfs / +0xbc lfs pair present in BOTH streams), the four-iteration Newton-Raphson body, the `d = dx*dx + dy*dy; d = dz*dz + d;` split and the loop's `i++, node += 104` step were held constant across both probes; each varied exactly one thing (the `register` storage class on the accumulator; the scope of the four block-local f32 temps).

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Read the four pre-loop constant loads in both streams and check whether retail's f0 is written by anything other than the accumulator seed anywhere in the body. If retail ever uses f0 as scratch inside the loop, f0 is not reserved and the whole framing is wrong. Measured 2026-09-03 over the full aligned view: retail writes f0 exactly twice, at +0x14 (the seed) and +0xcc (`fmr f0,f6`, the update), and never as loop scratch - the reservation is real.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the nine-versus-nine FPR count, the two f0 writes, the three constant registers and the accumulator update site were all read from the aligned raw view against the retail bytes over the whole 58-instruction body, not inferred.
hypothesis.statement: The reachable lever is the LIVE RANGE of the accumulator, not its storage class or its declaration position. In retail the seed load sits at +0x14 and the accumulator is live across the whole loop; f0 is chosen because nothing else in the loop body needs a register at the moment the seed is materialised. The untried axis is to change WHEN the accumulator becomes live - initialise `best_dist` from a value that is not a compile-time constant (so the seed is not hoisted into the pre-loop constant block), or introduce a use of it before the loop, and see whether the f0 reservation follows. A second untried axis is the pool one: making the four constants TU-shared named objects rather than per-function anonymous entries changes the pre-loop block MWCC has to schedule around, and that block is where all four register choices are made.
